703648.t: From διδάσκω (dĭdắskō, “to teach”). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀇𐀅𐀏𐀩 (di-da-ka-re).

703649.t: Causative reduplication of the root of ἐδάην (edắēn, “learned, taught”, aorist; not attested in the present) with inchoative suffix -σκω (-skō), from Proto-Hellenic *di-dəs-skō, from Proto-Indo-European *dens- (“to learn”).

703620.t: From διαφαίνω (dĭăphaínō, “to shine; to be manifest”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjectival suffix).

703653.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁ Proto-Hellenic *dúwo Ancient Greek δύο (dúo)redup.

703654.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dídōmi, from Proto-Indo-European *dédeh₃ti, reduplicated athematic present of *deh₃- (“to give”).

703622.t: From δια- (dia-, “through, between”) + φέρω (phérō, “to bring, carry”).

703613.t: From δια- (dia-, “dia-, through-”) + τρέφω (tréphō, “to breed, feed”).

703641.t: From δια- (dĭă-, “apart”) + ψάλμα (psắlmă, “psalm”); hence literally “apart from the psalm”.

703681.t: From διηγέομαι (dĭēgéomai, “set out in detail, describe”) + -σις (-sĭs).

703696.t: From δίκαιος (díkaios, “decent, righteous”) + -όω (-óō, “cause someone to be”, factitive verb suffix).

703697.t: From δικαιόω (dikaióō, “to set right, deem right”) + -μα (-mă).

703628.t: From δια- (dĭă-, “in different directions, asunder”) + φορέω (phoréō, “to wear; to hold, possess, bear”).
